questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am academically interested in Central and Eastern Europe, and Charles University offered courses with these topics. At the same time I had the possibility of trying to live in one of these countries.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay but could have been better.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing apart from a few emails from the international office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy as Charles University offered accommodation at a dormitory.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was a bit far from the university, but I really liked to stay at the dorm. I was easy to make friends there, and the price was very cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The dormitory looked very bad and old, and the facilities were not good. The staff was very rude. But a lot of good and sweet erasmus people lived there, so I would recommend anytime.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to wake up early in one of the first weeks during the stay, and be ready to register for the courses. It was a stressing process, as you had to rush a lot to get only some of the courses you wanted, as they quickly got filled up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Nothing. It could have been helpfull with an introduction on how to use the course registration system (sis)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got some of them, and some of them I did not get.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the courses upon the day of registration and save the course codes so that you can search them easily. Be ready when the registration opens, and the rest is luck.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was much lower than I am used to at UCPH. It was easy to pass most of the courses without putting a lot of effort.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UK we had to make presentations in order to pass courses, which I rarely experience at UCPH. At UCPH all my exams are long written essays, and at UK it was presentations, tests and oral exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Czech for advanced beginners
- Everyday Life Under Socialism: Strategies and Practices
- Geopolitical Importance of Central Europe
- Milestones of Modern Czech History (1848–1989)
- Modern History of Central Europe
- Political and Cultural History of Modern Afghanistan

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
- Czech for advanced beginners: I had two very good and sweet teachers who made a good environment for learning.

- Political and Cultural History of Modern Afghanistan: very good and passionate teacher. More thematically than the rest of the courses which was only about learning specific names and years. I learned a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Dentist, new screen for my phone because I broke it, paying for vacuum and laundry

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public transport was more cheap than expected. I can really recommend to buy a 3 months pass to save money. Fitness was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not look for it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not know. I did not look it up and I did not participate in anything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not participate in anything at the school. I can recommend going to the pub quizzes arranged by the Erasmus student organisation.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take a trip to Plzen and Terezin. Very recommendable.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy as it is very similar to Denmark (culturally, religiously). It also helped that I learned some Czech.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No. It do not know where to find them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I felt very safe in Prague, which I appreciated a lot. The prices are so cheap compared to Denmark, which gave me a lot of freedom in how I wanted to spend my time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Stay at one of the dormitories offered. You will make a lot of great international friends there, compared to staying in an apartment and only socialising with people from your own country. And it is cheap.
- Do not stress so much about deadlines and documents. Everything will be solved at the end.
- Be open for learning about other cultures. You may learn something new.
- Don't worry about your english level. You will adapt in a few days.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
- buy a 3 month pass in the "pid litacka" app for public transportation.
- Enjoy your time!!
- Book some trips around Europe. A lot of bus and plane tickets are cheap from Prague.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get a lot of international friends from other countries in Europe. These will be life long friendships, and they learned me a lot about myself, my own country, and theirs.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To fix formalities with the sending and hosting institution.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
